change: Replace the rounded-distance bucket hash map plus second priority queue in Occupancy::place_near_impl with an ordered deque. Raw frontier distances and exact decimal rounding are monotone, so bucket keys already arrive sorted.
invariants: Preserve raw frontier visitation, rounding calls, strict half-step flush condition, x/y ordering within each bucket, collision predicates, budget/result-cap semantics, accounting and emitted geometry. No legal candidate pruning or hardware policy changes.

tests.status: All PASS; subsequently expanded dense frontier tests also PASS.
tests.new_coverage: 75 dense-grid combinations: five steps, three conservative flush margins, and five anchors including adjacent binary64 values around a decimal boundary. Enumerate every physically legal pose independently, sort by rounded Manhattan distance/x/y, compare complete returned sequences and independently observed scalar receipts. Existing child/THT masks, bounded search and changing-blocker oracles remain covered.

benchmark.design: Three serial pairs for each board; orders before-after, after-before, before-after. Same executable target/compiler configuration, repository inputs, schematic input, host and CLI options. No agent build/test process ran concurrently during these pairs. Other host load was not controlled.

limitations: Modest observed model-time change with run-to-run variability; not a guaranteed speedup or full build/render/audit/compile timing. Text-emission times are separately recorded, including slower samples. No board area change or new full qualification. This compares two C++ versions only; the requested historical Python comparison remains outstanding.
